banner: Research context for analyst review — not a trading instruction.

input.raw_text: That CPI print was a gut punch. Nobody had 8.6 for the headline and the bond market did not waste a second: the ten-year backed up violently and the front end prices a seventy-five basis point hike this month as a live option rather than a tail. Stocks and bonds are down together — the configuration that hurts every balanced portfolio — and there is nowhere to hide; even gold is slipping as real yields rip. The Nasdaq is down hard because higher discount rates hurt long-duration assets most, but the selling is broad. The Fed has been explicit about needing deceleration, and this print guarantees a hawkish meeting. The tragedy is that positioning had finally built a thawing narrative — peak inflation, peak hawkishness — and the data just torched it. Until the two-year rolls over, equities are fighting gravity.
input.summary: An unexpectedly high 8.6% headline CPI reading triggered a sharp rise in Treasury yields, made a seventy-five-basis-point near-term rate increase appear more plausible, and coincided with broad declines across stocks, bonds, and gold. Nasdaq weakness was especially pronounced as higher real yields and discount rates weighed on long-duration assets. The release disrupted expectations for peak inflation and easing policy pressure, leaving the outlook for equities constrained while the two-year yield remains elevated.
